latest_nl_proof:
Since 0 <= b <= a <= n/2, we have d = a - b >= 0 and a = b + d. Also n - a >= a >= 0, so for every index that appears below, the exponents n-a+i, n-b+i, i, and b+i are positive integers. Hence all factors 1 - q^m that occur are nonzero polynomials, and the manipulations below are valid in the ambient field of rational functions in q.

By the definition of the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient,
[n choose a]_q / [n choose b]_q
= (prod_{i=1}^a ((1 - q^(n-a+i))/(1 - q^i))) / (prod_{i=1}^b ((1 - q^(n-b+i))/(1 - q^i)))
= ((prod_{i=1}^a (1 - q^(n-a+i))) (prod_{i=1}^b (1 - q^i))) / ((prod_{i=1}^a (1 - q^i)) (prod_{i=1}^b (1 - q^(n-b+i)))).

Now split the length-a products using a = b + d.
First,
prod_{i=1}^a (1 - q^(n-a+i))
= (prod_{i=1}^d (1 - q^(n-a+i))) (prod_{i=d+1}^{d+b} (1 - q^(n-a+i)))
= (prod_{i=1}^d (1 - q^(n-a+i))) (prod_{j=1}^b (1 - q^(n-a+d+j)))
= (prod_{i=1}^d (1 - q^(n-a+i))) (prod_{j=1}^b (1 - q^(n-b+j))),
where in the middle step we reindexed by j = i - d.

Second,
prod_{i=1}^a (1 - q^i)
= (prod_{i=1}^b (1 - q^i)) (prod_{j=1}^d (1 - q^(b+j))).

Substituting these two decompositions into the previous fraction gives
[n choose a]_q / [n choose b]_q
= ((prod_{i=1}^d (1 - q^(n-a+i))) (prod_{j=1}^b (1 - q^(n-b+j))) (prod_{i=1}^b (1 - q^i)))
  / ((prod_{i=1}^b (1 - q^i)) (prod_{j=1}^d (1 - q^(b+j))) (prod_{j=1}^b (1 - q^(n-b+j)))).

The identical b-factor products cancel, so
[n choose a]_q / [n choose b]_q
= (prod_{i=1}^d (1 - q^(n-a+i))) / (prod_{i=1}^d (1 - q^(b+i)))
= prod_{i=1}^d ((1 - q^(n-a+i))/(1 - q^(b+i))).

Finally, since A = n - a and B = b, this is exactly
prod_{i=1}^d ((1 - q^(A+i))/(1 - q^(B+i))).

If d = 0, then these are empty products, hence equal to 1, so the same identity also covers the case a = b. Therefore
[n choose a]_q / [n choose b]_q = prod_{i=1}^d ((1 - q^(A+i))/(1 - q^(B+i))),
with the right-hand side equal to 1 when d = 0, as claimed.
role_in_parent: Converts the reduced quotient into the consecutive-interval product form needed for the commutative-algebra model.
statement_nl: For integers n, a, b with 0 <= b <= a <= n/2, let d := a - b, A := n - a, and B := b. Define [n choose t]_q := prod_{i=1}^t (1 - q^(n-t+i)) / (1 - q^i), with the empty product equal to 1 when t = 0. Then [n choose a]_q / [n choose b]_q = prod_{i=1}^d (1 - q^(A+i)) / (1 - q^(B+i)), where the product is 1 if d = 0.

domain_restrictions: a ≤ n/2 (equivalently a ≤ n/2 and hence a ≤ n)
d := a - b is therefore an integer and d ≥ 0
A := n - a is an integer (no sign restriction stated)
B := b is an integer and B ≥ 0
Gaussian q-binomial [n choose t]_q is defined via products indexed by i=1..t; empty product convention applies when t=0
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: Under the constraints 0 ≤ b ≤ a ≤ n/2 for integers n,a,b, define d=a-b, A=n-a, B=b, and for any t≥0 define [n choose t]_q = ∏_{i=1}^t (1-q^(n-t+i)) / (1-q^i) (with ∏_{i=1}^0 = 1). Then [n choose a]_q / [n choose b]_q = ∏_{i=1}^d (1-q^(A+i)) / (1-q^(B+i)), with ∏_{i=1}^0 = 1 (i.e., the RHS product equals 1 when d=0).
quantifier_order: For all integers n, a, b such that 0 ≤ b ≤ a ≤ n/2
q is a parameter as used in the definitions (not explicitly quantified)
